$comment: Registry of upstream sources for the Florida Water Quality API.
`verified` is the important field. It means: this exact URL was reached by
`python -m fwq probe` and answered, and the result was recorded in
`data/water/source-probe.json`. Anything still false is a candidate that
has NOT been confirmed from this environment and must not be presented to
EPA Envirofacts is the backbone. Everything else is either a richer view of
the same federal data (ECHO, UCMR download files) or genuinely additive
state/utility data that has no federal equivalent (FDEP enforcement, CCRs,
Egress note: as of the last probe from the build container, data.epa.gov,
floridadep.gov, and prodenv.dep.state.fl.us were refused at the network
policy layer (HTTP 403 on CONNECT). CI runners are not subject to that
policy, which is why ingest runs in GitHub Actions.

sources.name: EPA Envirofacts SDWIS REST service
sources.notes: Primary inventory and violation source. No API key. Answers 404 for empty result sets.

sources.name: EPA UCMR 5 occurrence data (PFAS + lithium)
sources.notes: Table name has moved between UCMR cycles; the client probes several candidates. Bulk download fallback is epa-ucmr5-download.

sources.name: EPA UCMR 5 bulk data download page
sources.notes: Zipped fixed-width/CSV national files. Fallback when the Envirofacts UCMR 5 tables are unavailable.

sources.name: EPA ECHO Safe Drinking Water Act REST services
sources.notes: Adds enforcement actions and a rolled-up compliance history that SDWIS alone does not expose.

sources.name: Florida DEP Source and Drinking Water Program
sources.notes: Florida holds SDWA primacy, so FDEP is the agency whose data feeds federal SDWIS. Landing page only; not machine-readable.

sources.name: Florida DEP public water system facility search (WAFR)
sources.notes: CANDIDATE URL, not confirmed. FDEP's facility-level detail is richer and fresher than the federal SDWIS extract, but the search is form-driven. Confirm the endpoint and whether a machine-readable view exists before wiring an ingest.

sources.name: Florida DEP GIS open data / ArcGIS REST
sources.notes: CANDIDATE URL, not confirmed. Wanted for address-level service-area resolution, which ZIP mapping cannot do accurately.

sources.name: US Census Bureau geocoding API
sources.notes: Free, no key, already used elsewhere in this repo (water-leads/census_client.py). Turns an address into coordinates for the address -> utility path.

$comment: Florida has no statewide machine-readable boil-water-notice feed. Notices
are published per utility and per county health department, so each one
is registered individually with its own extraction strategy.
